figures.finding: Bahrain levies no income tax on individuals, so a resident's pay and fees bear none.

sources.said: Individual taxation There is no individual income tax.

figures.finding: A non-resident performer's or writer's fee bears no withholding: Bahrain has no withholding taxes in 2026 (a 5% withholding on service and royalty payments to companies has only been announced).

sources.said: Withholding tax There are no withholding taxes. Bahrain has announced it intends to introduce withholding tax on certain cross-border payments to corporate entities on Bahrain-source income. The rate would be 0% for dividend payments, and 5% for interest, royalty, and service payments.

figures.finding: Social insurance: for a Bahraini, the employee pays 8% (pension, disability, death, unemployment) and the employer a share stated as 15% that rises one point a year from 2024 to reach 20% in 2028; for an expatriate, the employer pays 3% (injuries) and the employee 1% (unemployment); earnings above BHD 4,000 a month are not counted.
figures.applies: Employees in Bahrain; the 2026 employer rate for Bahrainis is not settled by this source (15% stated, but a +1 point a year schedule from 2024 implies more).

sources.said: For Bahraini nationals, the employer’s social insurance contribution is 15% and the employee’s contribution is 8%, which covers old age, disability, death, and unemployment. The employer’s share will increase by one percentage point each year between 2024 and 2028, bringing the total percentage of the employer’s share to 20% in 2028. For expatriate employees, the employer’s social insurance contribution is 3%, which covers employment injuries. Expatriate employees contribute 1%, which covers unemployment. The maximum monthly earnings subject to contributions are capped at BHD 4,000.

figures.finding: A freelancer must register for VAT once annual taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed BHD 37,500 (voluntary from BHD 18,750); the standard rate is 10%.

sources.said: The standard rate is 10% and applies to most goods and services.

Registration: Businesses with an annual VAT taxable turnover exceeding or expected to exceed BHD 37,500 must register for VAT within 30 days of the date when the threshold is exceeded or expected to be exceeded. Taxable persons may voluntarily register for VAT if the annual VAT taxable turnover and/or annual expenses subject to VAT in Bahrain exceed or is expected to exceed BHD 18,750.

figures.finding: Under Law no. 14 of 2022, the pension branch of social insurance for a Bahraini costs the employer 17% and the employee 7% of monthly pay, reached in steps: 11% and 6% on the law's entry into force in 2022, the employee at 7% from the next year and the employer rising one point a year to 17%.
figures.applies: Bahraini employees; on a yearly step from 2022 the employer's pension share is 14% or 15% in 2026 by the step date (not stated by the law); unemployment and injury shares are in the Deloitte figure above; expatriates are under end-of-service, not the pension branch (art. 10).
